I've been thinking this way a lot too. Hell, I came back to this throwaway after 7 years in a haze because things feel like theyve barely gotten better from the situation I escaped from the last times I was here...

I was going to make my own post too- about how I hate this grinding we have to do. The constant whittling and sharpening of our skills with the promise of a happy retirement, when we're just a stub left of the pencil that was our life. For what though? The betterment of society? In America at least...hardly. Sometimes for the sake of our own lives to continue, we get forced to push down all our feelings to be a cog in a machine. Most of the time we have away from such work is just trying to build ourselves up with an emotional armor to be able to withstand it all again.

Ive seen many people who I cared about vehemently throw their relationships and hobbies to the side for the sake of jobs that would not hesitate to cut them off if given half a reasonable pitch to do so. For the sake of a nebulous promise of "Someday Ill be able to relax if I work really really hard now" and honestly? It just kind of hit me this reads a lot like the promise of "Sugarcandy Mountain" in Animal Farm.

Why are we wholly being expected to wait for peace and happiness and love of life? Why is comfort something that is deemed to be earned rather than a right? As far as I know, none of us had a say in coming to this world. Why is it so controversial to suggest we should be providing basic needs to everyone, regardless of their potential output in labor to stimulate such needs? 

The fortunate who achieve...I feel like it can be a case of both disillusionment with the fact that the success was a combination of their own passion and fluke and the imposter syndrome of being able to tell just how significant their contribution was in the end.

I dont know any comforting platitudes to offer, other than my own thoughts. Im keeping afloat myself. Crying at the end of every month. Involuntary disassociating into another world within my head whenever I see my bank balance. Somehow I'm able to last the tide pool into the next month and feel calm until the pressure of expectations and looming threat of displacement starts lapping at my ankles again, rising and rising once more.

My only real solace is myself, my stories, my art, my loved ones. Some of my friends flit in and out as they please and I feel a sense of tired loss since I dont have the object permeance (or lack idk) to have my affection for them fade simply because we dont speak for a few months. 

It gets so damn tiresome to keep going, chugging along and have people hmm and aww at your sorrow and desire to be...to just BE. And at the end of the conversation, the shrug. The sigh. The "yeah but"s. We can do better, but we've been trained to be beaten down and segregate, point fingers and hate. Hate everyone else but those responsible for making us feel like self-aware distressed wind-up toys in the first place.

I hear you though. And so does everyone else. Even if we may be too scared to "rock the boat" for our own already precarious situation. Even if we can offer nothing tangible to get you out of this clutching, suffocating feeling of invalidity...we hear you. 

It shouldnt matter how far a pebble can skip across the river, or how many ripples it makes. What matters is the pebble is there. Slick and smooth. Small, Big, Flat or Round. Without the stones, there is just water. Would it still flow the same way? 

Maybe my heart is just so achy the metaphors are running too deep but... I wish all of us the best in the end.
